title: Entropy-based triage framework for air-gapped / restricted-network private deploy requests
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem statement:
Customers requesting Private/VPC/on-prem deployments frequently submit requests with highly variable network constraints, upgrade tolerances, and legal/compliance constraints. Current intake is manual, slow, and tends to bottleneck on ambiguous network readouts or missing upgrade windows. That increases time-to-onboard, surprises engineering during preflight, and drives expensive escalations.

Goal:
Build a lightweight, explainable triage framework that scores incoming private-deploy requests on an "entropy" index (degree of unknowns + risk surface) and maps them into deterministic engagement lanes: Low-touch (self-serve), Assisted (SRE/SE-run), Fasttrack (contracted dedicated gate), and Blocked (requires legal/compliance remediation). The score should be computable from customer-submitted answers + automated probes and should feed routing rules, SLA promises, and a templated comms playbook.

Scope for this ticket:
1) Define the entropy scoring rubric and per-signal weights (network topology unknowns, firewall policy opacity, airgap status, upgrade window flexibility, third-party dependency risk, data residency constraints).
2) Author deterministic lane definitions and required artifacts per lane (e.g., manifest, network probes, temporary proxy access, approved legal addendum).
3) Create sample comms templates for each lane (sales/CS + engineering) including cost & timeline ranges.
4) Prototype a serverless triage function that computes the score and returns lane + explanation (no full automation of self-serve in this ticket).
5) Document acceptance criteria and handoff plan for ENG + SRE to implement scoring in the intake form and Console.

Trade-offs considered:
- Accuracy vs speed: heavier probe suites increase accuracy but delay triage and are more invasive. We favor an initial fast score (low overhead) with an optional deep-probe step for mid-entropy requests.
- Explainability vs complexity: keep scoring linear and auditable; avoid opaque ML blackboxes in the initial release to support customer trust and legal review.
- Customer experience: prefer conservative lane placement with clear remediation steps rather than optimistic auto-approval.
acceptance_criteria: Defined entropy rubric with at least 8 signals and assigned weights (documented)
Mapping table from score ranges to engagement lanes and required artifacts
Comms templates for Sales/CS/Engineering with time and cost brackets
Prototype triage function returning {score, lane, explanation} and test harness with 10 synthetic example requests
Handoff doc for ENG/SRE + backlog tickets for integration into intake form and Console routing
comments: 2025-02-20 Priya Nair: Created ticket after portfolio review — several inbound enterprise requests stalled due to unclear firewall topology and upgrade window mismatch. Framing as entropy to capture observed uncertainty patterns.

2025-02-24 Mateo Gonzalez: Scoped signals during PM-ENG sync. Proposed initial signals: declared network topology, inbound/outbound port openness, egress proxy requirement, jump-host availability, upgrade blackout windows, legal addendum status, data residency, and third-party SaaS webhooks. Agreed to weight upgrade blackout highly.

2025-02-28 Sarah Park (Eng): Confirmed feasibility of lightweight network probe (TCP/443 reachability, TTL traceroute) for Assisted lane; flagged corporate security concerns for active probes in air-gapped customers — will need customer opt-in or offline probe artifacts.

2025-03-03 Legal (M. O'Neill): Review note — any automated scoring that gates commercial commitment must have an appeals channel; suggested including explicit 'manual review' bucket for high legal risk and logging rationale in audit trail.
2025-03-05 Mateo Gonzalez: Drafted lane definitions and comms templates; attached initial cost delta matrix (one-time onboarding engineering hours + optional proxy connector fee).

2025-03-10 Design review with Emily Bryant: Prefer inline explanation snippets in intake UI with simple remediation checkboxes; avoid long legalese. Design will produce low-fidelity UI microcopy by 2025-03-17.

2025-03-12 Priya Nair: Updated acceptance criteria to require 10 synthetic request examples across low/medium/high entropy and attached to test harness. Next: schedule triage rubric review with Sales leaders and SRE on 2025-03-18.
